test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the 2025 Global Hunger Index report, what is India’s rank among the assessed countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**102nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **2025 Global Hunger Index (GHI)** report, **India** has been ranked **102nd** out of the **127 countries** that were assessed.
 
• India’s performance is categorized under the **"Serious"** level of hunger, with a specific **GHI score** that reflects the ongoing challenges in nutrition and food security. ***Hence, the statement regarding the rank is correct.***
 
• The report is a peer-reviewed annual publication produced by two international NGOs: **Concern Worldwide** (based in **Ireland**) and **Welthungerhilfe** (based in **Germany**).
 
• The **2025** ranking shows a slight improvement in India's position compared to the previous year (**2024**), where it was ranked **105th** out of **127** nations.
 
• The report highlights that while India has made strides in certain areas, the levels of **child wasting** and **undernourishment** remain significant concerns for policy makers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Four Indicators of GHI:**

 
 
• **Undernourishment**: This measures the share of the entire population with **insufficient caloric intake**.
 
• **Child Stunting**: This refers to the share of **children under age five** who have low height for their age, reflecting **chronic undernutrition**.
 
• **Child Wasting**: This indicates the share of **children under age five** who have low weight for their height, reflecting **acute undernutrition**.
 
• **Child Mortality**: The **mortality rate** of children under the age of five, partially reflecting the fatal mix of inadequate nutrition and unhealthy environments.
 
 
 
• **Scoring Methodology:**
 
 
• The GHI determines hunger on a **100-point scale**, where **0** is the best possible score (no hunger) and **100** is the worst.
 
• Values less than **9.9** are considered **low**, **10.0–19.9** are **moderate**, **20.0–34.9** are **serious**, **35.0–49.9** are **alarming**, and above **50.0** are **extremely alarming**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Comparisons:** In the **2025** report, several of India’s neighbors, including **Bangladesh**, **Nepal**, and **Sri Lanka**, often rank higher (better) than India, despite having smaller economies. **Pakistan** generally ranks close to or lower than India in these assessments.
 
• **Government Perspective:** The **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in India has frequently questioned the **methodology** of the GHI. The government argues that the index relies heavily on **opinion polls** and that the **sample size** is too small to represent a country of **1.4 billion people**.
 
• **Child Wasting in India:** India historically reports one of the **highest rates of child wasting** in the world, a metric that significantly pulls down its overall GHI ranking.
 
• **Global Context:** The **2025** report emphasizes that global progress against hunger has largely stagnated since **2015**, due to **climate change**, **conflicts**, and **economic shocks**.
